On a lateral view, one can assess kyphosis (anterior-posterior curvature) but not left/right scoliosis directly because the vertebrae are superimposed in the sagittal plane. However, sometimes rotation or specific vertebral body shapes might hint at underlying scoliosis, or the question might be testing knowledge that this view *cannot* show it, or perhaps there is a subtle sign I am missing.
